standard_prerequisites.name: Set-level quotient and effectivity
standard_prerequisites.statement: A relation R:A->A->prop is effective when the kernel pair of the quotient map is exactly the relation with respect to the quotient identification.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the property the statement claims for the kernel relation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Image as a set-quotient
standard_prerequisites.statement: im(f) is the set of pairs (b, |a,_|) with f(a)=b, i.e. the image of f as a subset of B.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof constructs the comparison map c_f:A->im(f) and studies its kernel pair.

standard_prerequisites.name: Kernel of a function
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation that the theorem proves effective.

core_obligations: Use that im(f) is the coequalizer of the two projections from sum_{x,y:A} f(x)=f(y) to A, so that the kernel pair of c_f is the displayed relation (source lines 392-402).

Compute the type c_f(x)=c_f(y) by passing to the total space of the equality family, using that the fibre of f is a mere proposition to collapse the two summands, obtaining an equivalence with f(x)=f(y) for all x,y:A (source lines 403-410).
Conclude that sum_{x,y:A} c_f(x)=c_f(y) is equivalent to sum_{x,y:A} f(x)=f(y), hence that ker(f) is an effective relation (source lines 411-416).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the kernel pair of the comparison map c_f:A->im(f) with the two projections out of the sum of the equality family.
First collapse the equality in im(f) to an equality in the total space, then use that the fibre of f is a mere proposition.
Assemble the equivalence of kernel pairs and read off effectivity of ker(f).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Proposition 10.1.9 at source lines 385-389: for any function f:A->B between sets, the relation ker(f,x,y) defined as f(x)=f(y) is effective. The author's proof (source lines 391-417) runs on the comparison map c_f(a) = (f(a), |a,refl|) into the image and on the kernel pair of that map. The two identifications that have to be carried out are not routine: the type c_f(x)=c_f(y) is first rewritten as a sum over p:f(x)=f(y) with a transported truncation on each side, and the collapse of that sum uses the fact that the fibre of f is a mere proposition; one then has to see that the resulting equivalence of kernel pairs is precisely effectivity. The statement records only the relation and the conclusion, and neither the comparison map nor the mere-proposition step appears in it.
